### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **33** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via buildMcpBridge (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-5.mdx`  _(via IActionConfirmationService (symbol, a top-level type), pending_confirmation (literal, a string literal in a comment in McpActionBridge; a string literal in a comment on a changed line; a string literal in handOffActionConfirmation; a string literal in registerActionTools))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **37** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dfb8ed3570b3be1cfbc3758ff791ace7c31fa1a2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `539252eb6acea48618504016070adb63fca92424` — the merge of head `a18a85ca6e1b65ace8c22d2e79a44412c102a70a` into base `dfb8ed3570b3be1cfbc3758ff791ace7c31fa1a2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 539252eb6acea48618504016070adb63fca92424 && git checkout 539252eb6acea48618504016070adb63fca92424
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin dfb8ed3570b3be1cfbc3758ff791ace7c31fa1a2 a18a85ca6e1b65ace8c22d2e79a44412c102a70a && git checkout -B drift-repro dfb8ed3570b3be1cfbc3758ff791ace7c31fa1a2 && git merge --no-ff a18a85ca6e1b65ace8c22d2e79a44412c102a70a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dfb8ed3570b3be1cfbc3758ff791ace7c31fa1a2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs dfb8ed3570b3be1cfbc3758ff791ace7c31fa1a2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `292c638502c81c2d62204640365ffd1c715afa83`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-confirmation-handoff-33690.test.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-action-confirmation-handoff-33690.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/action-confirmation-handoff-33690.dogfood.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-confirmation-gate.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/mcp-resume-run.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/api-action-forward.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/mcp-system-object-action-exposure.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/platform-admin-action-gate.test.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-resume-run-tool.test.ts, examples/app-todo/test/mcp-actions.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/approval-decide-over-mcp.dogfood.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/approval-read-over-mcp.dogfood.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/mcp-system-object-action-exposure.dogfood.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/mcp-delete-record-confirmation.dogfood.test.ts + packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.action-requires-confirmation-elicited.ts, packages/runtime/src/flow-start-admission.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts, packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/tool.zod.ts, .github/workflows/ci.yml (all read, not reviewed)

Read: card #33690 body and its four comments (triage 6890545596, re-sequencing 6890862846, claim 6898081431, dev report 6904293454), the PR body, the net diff `86350e12..292c6385` (20 files, +1360/-293), and the check-runs on the head. Every completed check-run on the head is `success` or `skipped`; both `Check Changeset` runs are `success`.

### ① Derived judgments

Each change the diff implies, judged against the tree:

- **`run_action`, gated action, `confirm: true` no longer runs it** — right. `invokeBusinessAction` no longer passes `confirmation: input`; it sets `confirmationHandOff`, and `admitResolvedAction` takes the `aiDoorConfirmation` branch, which has no request parameter and so cannot read the member in any spelling.
- **`resume_run`, same** — right. `resumeAdmissionRefusal` lost its `request` parameter; the hand-off runs after steps 4 and 5 (`refuseUnresumableAdmittedRun`), and the run stays parked.
- **New successful answer `status: 'pending_confirmation'` on both tools** — right. It matches `ActionConfirmationPending` in the spec, and the tool relays it through `textResult` as a non-error result.
- **`428` details gain `reason`** (`no_confirmation_service` at MCP; `service_account` for an account at every action door, REST and the host door included) — right. Additive, from the spec's closed set, and the changeset says so.
- **The confirmation step moves after the subject load for a non-account caller** — right, by contract step 2. A gated call on a record the caller cannot read now answers `404` where it answered `428`, and a refused call may have read its subject. An account is still refused before the load.
- **No `action_invocation` row for a hand-off** — right. The call did not run; the contract makes the pending item the host's record.
- **`confirm` stays in both input schemas, unread** — right for this card; no schema narrowing is published. Its retirement is open question B (③).
- **No public export moves.** `packages/runtime/src/index.ts` exports only `dispatchAction` and its three types from these files; `ResolvedActionRun` gaining `handedOff` is internal.
- **Pre-forward refusals of an `api`-typed gated action** (the `sys_api_key` guard, organization-role endpoints) are now answered by the confirmation step first — right. They sit in the forward, after admission; the pins keep the guard on an ungated twin.

Flipped pins: I read all eleven existing test files against the dev report's `flipped_pins`. Each moves only what the declaration says:
- "runs on `confirm: true`" becomes "refused `no_confirmation_service` with and without the member";
- account refusals gain `reason: 'service_account'`;
- the dropped "reads no record" assertion in `action-confirmation-gate.test.ts` follows from the reordering above;
- the delete-gate parity pin sets `reason` aside and asserts the delete gate carries none.

No pin outside the confirmation behaviour was loosened. The REST, host-door and ungated controls are kept or added.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: semantic` appear line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset.
- `semantic` is right: no key or accepted value is added or removed; what an author's `ai.requiresConfirmation: true` means at the MCP door changes.
- `minor` on `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/mcp` is right: a kind other than `none` takes at least `minor` on each package the diff moves, and those are the two it moves (the `examples` and `qa` hunks are tests).
- Narrowing-arm obligations, all present:
  - `!` in the title;
  - the **BREAKING** banner with FROM and TO lines in the changeset;
  - exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (already-registered action-requires-confirmation-elicited)`; the entry exists at the merge base and its surface is this declaration.
- The dogfood battery obligation is judged in ③.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Battery not re-run after the two test-only commits — acceptable on the evidence, but not for the reason the PR body gives.**
  - The full battery ran at `56a42d81e2` with 2 red files, both consequences of this change.
  - `56a42d81..292c6385` touches three test files only (+11/-4); no source moved. Both red dogfood files are reported green at the head, and the third is a runtime unit file covered by `Test Core` on the head.
  - CI did **not** run the battery on this head. `Dogfood Regression Gate (shard/3)` is `skipped` on every `pull_request` run by design (`ci.yml`, the shard job's `if:`), and the bare `Dogfood Regression Gate` `success` is the aggregate over a skipped matrix. It is not a battery result.
  - The shards run in the merge queue, where the context is required. The seat's pre-queue check ("pinned to head, full") is met in substance by the union above, not by the letter. Recorded as an accepted deviation (nit); the seat may instead ask for one re-run at the head, which moves nothing.
- **Open question (retire `confirm` from the two input schemas)**: escalated, not answered here. It is a further narrowing beyond ruling 6890862846 and is carried on #34209 for the maintainer.
- **Deviations in the dev report**:
  - Editing `action-dispatch.ts` and `domains/mcp.ts` is within the claim's "runtime wiring"; the hand-off cannot sit after the verdict otherwise.
  - Flipping pins outside the new files is what the claim's "tests pinning the opposite flip" says.
  - The no-service message omits "use a client that supports confirmation", which contract step 3 names. Accepted: no door elicits until #33712, so the sentence would be false today.
- **Out-of-scope findings** are carried: #34209 (served skill and `TOOL_RETIRED_KEY_GUIDANCE`), #34212 (flow-start `reason` parity), #34214 (scenario grader), #34210 (skills).

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real.** The contract on `main` (`AI_ACTION_CONFIRMATION_CAPABILITY`, `ai-service.ts`) already says the caller's `confirm` never counts on a declared-gated call at `run_action` and `resume_run`, and that the doors enforce it "in the change that enforces it". This is that change. Elicitation (step 1) is declared and not delivered; that is a tracked implementation gap (#33712, re-sequenced by ruling 6890862846), and the fallback taken is step 2 or 3, never the member.

Attempts to break the hand-off, all failed:
- **Other doors.** `buildMcpBridge` in `domains/mcp.ts` is the only `McpActionBridge` implementation, so stdio and HTTP share the one path. `runResolvedAction` has two callers: the MCP door (hand-off) and the REST renderer (never sets `confirmationHandOff`). No other MCP tool runs an action.
- **REST `/actions`, the host door under `ai`, flow starts**: unchanged, as the contract's bounds and the card say; pinned by three controls.
- **Spellings of `confirm`.** The hand-off branch takes no request. A non-boolean top-level value fails the tool schema, and `params.confirm` meets the param contract.
- **A service that throws, or misbehaves.**
  - `submit` rejecting propagates and nothing dispatches.
  - A missing or empty `pendingId` throws.
  - A resolution that throws, or a registration without `submit`, reads as no service and answers `428`.
  - Every case fails closed.
- **Account and delegated agent.** An account is refused before the subject load and never handed off; a delegated agent is handed off for its person.
- **Multi-candidate `resume_run`.** The first admitted candidate decides; a gated candidate that used to be skipped without `confirm` now hands off, which is stricter, never looser.

Findings:

1. **should-fix — the served skill still teaches the member.** `packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts` (lines 480-502, published in the package this PR marks BREAKING) and `TOOL_RETIRED_KEY_GUIDANCE` in `packages/spec/src/ai/tool.zod.ts` still tell an agent to send `confirm: true` on `run_action` and `resume_run`. The contract's "When it binds" says the enforcing change "also moves the shipped prescriptions that describe the member". Nothing runs wrongly; on a host with a service, an agent taught to retry creates a second pending item for the person. Carrier #34209 exists; it must ship in the same release as this changeset and takes its own review. No head move is asked of this PR.
2. **nit — migration entry wording.** Entry `action-requires-confirmation-elicited` keys its switch on "the release whose changelog says the AI doors confirm by elicitation", and this changeset says the doors do not elicit yet. A reader could conclude the switch has not happened. Fold into #34209.
3. **nit — bridged registry tools are outside this change.** `bridgeTools` (`mcp-server-runtime.ts`) serves a host AI service's `ToolRegistry` over the long-lived MCP server and runs each tool through the registry's own `execute`. The open build registers no such service, and the contract names only `run_action` and `resume_run`. Whether a host's action-backed tools take the hand-off is the host's; not measured here. Worth one card on the host side.
4. **nit — no pin for a rejecting `submit`**, and a resolution fault reads as "no pending-confirmation service" in the message. Both fail closed.
5. **nit — changeset `Skills-docs:` line** still reads "follow-up owed … rewrites it to #N" while the PR body names #34210; the line ships in `CHANGELOG.md`.
6. **nit — the hand-off does not ask the arm's own start refusals** (a flow's `requiredPermissions`, the `api` forward guards), so a person can be asked to approve a call that is refused on approval. The contract re-checks every gate at approval, so nothing runs.

**Contract face:** a declared narrowing, so the whole diff is under the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` record, comment 6904719554 (PASS, `Local-runs: none`). This ACCEPT read adopts it and adds the two items below.

**Owed**

1. **Before landing (prose only, a delta review of the changeset).** The changeset's `Skills-docs:` line still reads "follow-up owed … (the area files the card and rewrites it to #N)". That is release text with a placeholder in it. Rewrite it to `follow-up #34210`, as the PR body already says.
2. **Before the next release (carried by #34209, no head move here).** The record's should-fix applies: the MCP server's own served skill (`packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`) and `TOOL_RETIRED_KEY_GUIDANCE` still tell an agent that the server refuses a `requiresConfirmation` action without `confirm: true`. This PR makes that false, because the door hands the action off. An AI agent reads that text from the server it is talking to, so #34209 has to land in the same release as this changeset. Name that dependency on #34209.

**What holds (from the record, checked where named)**

- **Every MCP door takes the hand-off.** `buildMcpBridge` is the only action bridge, so stdio and HTTP share one path, and the hand-off branch reads no request field, so no spelling of `confirm` reaches it. If the service throws, returns no `pendingId` or has no `submit`, the door fails closed. With no service the answer is `428 ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` with reason `no_confirmation_service`. REST `/actions`, the host door and flow starts are left unchanged, within the bounds the contract states.
- **Flipped pins.** The eleven existing files move only what the declaration says.
- **Declaration.** The title has `!` and the changeset has a BREAKING banner with FROM → TO. The ADR-0087 marker is right. `semantic` is right. `runtime` and `mcp` take `minor`. Retiring `confirm` from the input schemas is the maintainer's open question on #34209 and is outside this PR.
- **The battery.** CI's `Dogfood Regression Gate` success on this head does not count as the battery: it is the aggregate over a shard matrix that `pull_request` runs skip. What covers this head is the full local battery at `56a42d81e2`, a test-only delta of three files since then, and both previously red files green at the head. The shards run again in the merge queue. I accept that.

**Nits (no re-review needed)**

These are the record's five:
- the migration entry's "doors confirm by elicitation" wording;
- the host AI service's tool registry is not routed (that is a host-side card);
- there is no pin for a rejecting `submit`;
- the stale changeset `Skills-docs:` line, which is item 1 above;
- start refusals are re-checked only at approval.

**Gates:** at review time 38 success, 18 skipped, none red.
